transcript.text: f/f freezer keeps icing up bottom drawer wont shut proper, defrosted it 2wks ago already full of ice again. indesit

Since the ice has returned so quickly after a manual defrost, this points to either a blocked drain hole or a failure in the automatic defrost system. To help me narrow this down and find the right part if needed, could you please provide the model number? It is usually on a sticker inside the fridge compartment (often on the side wall near the salad drawer).
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
its IB55532W, read it off the rating plate. indesit

Thanks for the model number. Since the ice has returned so quickly after a manual defrost, we are looking at either a blocked drain hole (which causes water to pool and freeze) or a failure in the automatic defrost system (like the heater or thermostat). To tell them apart, please perform a full manual defrost: switch it off at the socket, move food into cool bags, put towels down, and leave the doors open until every bit of ice has melted. Once clear, check for the small drain hole at the bottom of the back wall inside the freezer section. Is that hole blocked or frozen solid?
its a static freezer, no auto defrost i think. havent done the full defrost again yet. the door seal looks split at the bottom corner tho, want me to check that?

Yes, that is very likely the cause. Since you haven't done a full defrost yet, please do that first (switch off, empty food into cool bags, leave doors open until all ice melts). If the paper test shows poor suction at the bottom corner, the seal is most likely letting air in and needs replacing.
paper test already done, slides straight out at the bottom corner, grips elsewhere. seal split about 5cm and flattened at the hinge side. whats the part to search for?
You need a replacement door seal (gasket). Search for "Indesit IB55532W door seal" or use the model number on any appliance parts website.
